ideas.pitch: An acoustic off-grid messaging mesh network optimized for underground transit systems like the NYC subway, utilizing walkie-talkies and ultrasonic audio pulses for station-to-station data hopping.
ideas.title: SubwaySound Mesh
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows the proven physical build pattern from ICHack where hardware-adjacent networking stood out dramatically against standard web apps.

ideas.pitch: An offline AI code review hook running locally on device via NPUs or lightweight runtimes that flags vulnerabilities and bad commits without sending proprietary code to the cloud.
ideas.title: LocalLlama GitGuardian
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the offline AI architecture that won the Qualcomm Snapdragon Multiverse Hackathon, appealing to developer tooling and local privacy judges.

ideas.pitch: A computer vision garbage classification edge device built with a camera and microcontroller to automatically categorize NYC street waste for local composting and recycling compliance.
ideas.title: MetroScan AI Waste Sorter
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly matches the winning physical robotics and AI classification pattern seen at TechnoMorph Hackathon with a local NYC angle.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous multi-agent diagnostic platform that monitors simulated municipal water pipe sensor data, running anomaly detection loops to alert operators before leaks cause street flooding.
ideas.title: UrbanPipe Multi-Agent Ops
ideas.why_it_could_win: Adapts the complex multi-agent anomaly detection architecture that secured 3rd place at SEAL Hackathon into a localized municipal infrastructure utility.

ideas.pitch: A governable counter-UAS edge display system featuring a deterministic engagement gate and human-in-the-loop controls, keeping LLMs strictly off the critical decision path.
ideas.title: Aegis-City Drone Interceptor Gate
ideas.why_it_could_win: Employs the exact high-integrity safety architecture that won Best Collaboration at the AWS Global Government Hackathon by proving safe defense-tech constraint handling.
